first_choice.summary: Choose a settled (non-animated / non-flickering) information layout whose reading order is carried by explicit annotation ROLES (readable data value / illustrative decoration / no-label baseline) and a measurable static salience budget, not by style tokens and not by temporal blinking. Output a deterministic HTML layout plus a JSON spec and a small local self-check.
why_this_is_my_actual_first_choice: The hard task constraints are a NEW subject, UNCLEAR information hierarchy, and a ban on high-frequency flicker. A no-flicker scheme satisfies the <=3 Hz rule with zero flashing elements (0 Hz everywhere), removing the need to budget a temporal frequency I cannot verify without a render channel.

The unclear-hierarchy problem is structural, not stylistic: conflicts.md N4 says rules acting on the same pixel statistic are non-separable, while separable object CLASSES can be split with an explicit ownership table (N3) and per-layer budgets (N8/C-09). The three annotation roles are exactly three separable object classes.

The roktim___ seed mechanism_summary in CAPABILITIES.json literally separates 'readable data values, illustrative decoration and no-label baseline' — a role-based (semantic) hierarchy, which is the natural counter-example to a 'pure style' verdict.

Determinism contract C1-C8 (no real-time clocks, pure function of time, no CSS transitions, seeded randomness only) is satisfiable with a STATIC layout without any capture harness or image-generation service, all of which are unavailable in Stage A.

mechanism.definition: Assign each visible element exactly one of three roles. Only the readable data value may hold the single highest-salience slot. Salience is a declared, computable function of static, per-slot numbers (contrast ratio, area fraction, weight, accent flag) — never of temporal frequency. Keeping style tokens (palette, typeface, spacing) IDENTICAL while changing only the semantic role-to-slot binding is the contrast that can refute a 'pure style' explanation.

flicker_policy.constraint: <= 3 Hz for every flashing element; satisfied by having NO flashing or animated element (all frequencies 0 Hz). No opacity toggling, no keyframe animation, no CSS transition, no requestAnimationFrame.
flicker_policy.why_allowed: The task explicitly allows choosing a no-flicker scheme.

contrast_that_refutes_pure_style.held_constant: palette, type family, spacing scale, slot set (S1/S2/S3 with fixed contrast/area/weight/accent numbers)
contrast_that_refutes_pure_style.changed: only the binding of semantic role -> slot
contrast_that_refutes_pure_style.role_based_variant: readable data value -> S1 (top salience); illustration -> S2; no-label baseline -> S3
contrast_that_refutes_pure_style.pure_style_variant: illustration -> S1; readable data value -> S2; no-label baseline -> S3 (identical style vocabulary)
contrast_that_refutes_pure_style.prediction: If legibility were pure style, both variants would read identically. The check measures which ROLE occupies the top-salience slot: role_based => data_value (PASS); pure_style => illustration (FAIL). A legibility difference under constant style but changed role binding refutes 'pure style'. This is a MECHANICAL/declared contrast, NOT a human reading test.

alternatives_considered_and_not_chosen.what: Use C-09 / van Gogh star rule 'flicker period 0.8-1.5 s' (0.67-1.25 Hz, formally <=3 Hz) plus full-field swirl as the attention mechanism.
alternatives_considered_and_not_chosen.why_not: Full-field motion is exactly what conflicts.md C-09 contrasts with a single event region; adding a field of moving stars to an ALREADY unclear hierarchy increases motion noise rather than clarifying read order. structure.md requires motion to serve the verification anchor, not obscure it. Needs a render channel I do not have in Stage A (CAPABILITIES: supported=0; van Gogh web10s=untested). Not chosen even though its period would pass 3 Hz.

alternatives_considered_and_not_chosen.what: 07 sci-fi HUD style 'state change repaints whole scene cyan->warm' (mg-styles-15 compare L88).
alternatives_considered_and_not_chosen.why_not: A state-driven repaint is a temporal event whose repeat rate is unspecified; enforcing <=3 Hz would require a frame budget and a capture harness I cannot verify here. It is also itself a style pattern, i.e. the very thing under test, so it cannot serve as the mechanism that refutes 'pure style'.

alternatives_considered_and_not_chosen.what: Blink the key value rapidly to make it salient.
alternatives_considered_and_not_chosen.why_not: Explicitly disallowed (>3 Hz) and, per C-09/N8, temporal salience competes with a single-event motion budget; adds hierarchy noise.
